observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a black monocrystalline solar panel (all-black cells and frame), photographed outdoors against a wall/fence.
A reflection of a person taking the photo and heavy glare cover much of the panel surface in both shots.
A watermark reading 'Innoson Global Group' appears across both images; this is a reseller/poster watermark, not a manufacturer brand plate.
No specification sticker, wattage label, serial number, or manufacturer nameplate is legible in either photo.
No battery, inverter, or charge controller is visible in either photo, despite the seller's text mentioning these items.

claims.claim: High Quality Solar Panels, Inverters, Lithium & Tubular Batteries, Charge...
claims.evidence: Generic shop advertisement text; no corresponding photos of inverters, lithium or tubular batteries, or charge controllers were provided.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: No battery is shown in photo 0 or photo 1 — both images show only a solar panel, so this claim cannot refer to the pictured item.

risks.risk: Unknown wattage/model, which drives most of a solar panel's price.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rear junction-box specification sticker showing wattage, Voc/Isc, and model number.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common wattage tier for this physical size/type

risks.risk: Panel could be used/refurbished and relabeled rather than new, since glare hides surface condition.
risks.proof: Daylight photo without glare showing full cell surface, corners, and frame for cracks or hotspot stains.

risks.risk: Seller's text references a battery that is not depicted, raising doubt about what is actually being sold or whether photos match the advertised item.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the actual battery (brand, capacity label, terminals) if a battery is the item for sale, or confirmation that only the panel is for sale.
risks.if_unproven: treated as panel-only listing; battery claim excluded from price

risks.risk: No proof panel actually outputs rated power.
risks.proof: Video or photo of a multimeter/clamp meter reading under sunlight.

proof_requests: Clear, glare-free photo of the rear specification sticker (wattage, model, serial number).
Clarify whether the battery mentioned in the text is actually for sale, and if so, provide its own photos.
Daylight photo of the full panel surface without reflections to check for cracks, discoloration, or micro-fractures.
A multimeter or clamp-meter reading under sunlight to confirm output.
response.reason: The photos only show a solar panel with no legible wattage/model plate, and the seller's claim about a 'new battery holding charge 8 hours' does not match anything pictured, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without a spec-label photo and clarification of what is actually for sale.
